title: Engulfing + RVOL in Pine v6: breakout/retest entries and what the volume grades actually showed
author: Dependent-Ad6636

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: printing "probability untested" right on the panel is more honest than most scripts that get posted here. the 2023-24 loss on the same settings is the most useful line in the write-up, and I'd guess the high-volume shorts losing says more about gold trending up hard through that stretch than about volume.

replies.author: Dependent-Ad6636
replies.body:
Thanks, I appreciate that. Showing the losing period alongside the profitable one was important to me.

Your point about gold’s trend is plausible. High-volume shorts losing doesn’t by itself tell us whether volume added anything. A useful next check would be to compare RVOL grades within the same trade direction and predefined trend regime, keeping the sample sizes visible. Until then, I’m comfortable calling them volume grades, but not win probabilities.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
same direction plus a fixed trend filter is the right cut, though the high volume short bucket gets thin fast, so I'd print the n on every cell.

if you want a second run of it, I built Quantradin (quantradin.com), free and paper only. paste the Pine script in and it runs the rules on stocks and ETFs (GLD, not gold futures)

replies.author: Dependent-Ad6636
replies.body:
Good point on n—I’d show the count in every cell and avoid drawing conclusions from the thin buckets.

Thanks for sharing Quantradin, too! A GLD run could be an interesting additional check. I’d keep those results separate from the original gold test, though, since changing the instrument means it wouldn’t be a direct replication.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: agreed, separate run and separate write-up. a GLD result that disagrees with the gold one would be interesting all by itself.
